title: How to Get Your Ex Back: An Honest Step-by-Step Guide — cv.cm
description: How to get your ex back without games: when trying makes sense, what to change first, one honest message to send, how to read the reply, and when to stop.
h1: How do you get your ex back?
answer: Nobody can make an ex come back, and any page that promises it is selling something. What you can do is take space for at least a few weeks, understand honestly why it ended, change the part that was yours, then send one calm, honest message. If they say yes, go slowly and talk about the old problems. If they say no, accept it.

body: Wanting an ex back is very common. In Chinese it is called 挽回, in Japanese 復縁, in Vietnamese níu kéo. Many people search for a method that works on the other person. This page does not give one, because a relationship that restarts through pressure or tricks usually ends again, often worse.
Here is what is actually in your control:

ul: Whether you give both of you real space before you reach out.
Whether you understand why it ended, in their words and not only yours.
Whether you change your own behavior, and keep that change for months.
Whether your message is honest, short and free of pressure.
Whether you accept their answer.

body: What is not in your control: their feelings, their timing, and whether they have already moved on. A good outcome is either a second relationship that is better than the first, or a clear answer that lets you heal. Both are better than months of guessing.

sections.h: Should you even try? Why it ended matters most
body: Before you plan anything, look at the real reason for the breakup. Some problems can be fixed by two willing people. Some cannot, and some should not be fixed by getting back together at all.

One of you truly changes a goal for your own reasons, not to keep the other

body: The Gottman Institute describes four patterns that predict relationships ending: criticism, contempt, defensiveness and stonewalling (shutting down). If your fights were full of these, getting back together without learning a new way to argue will usually bring the same breakup back.

body.note: If the relationship had fear in it, such as threats, hitting, checking your phone, cutting you off from friends, or anger you had to manage, it was not a normal breakup and it is not your fault. Do not try to win that person back. Talk to someone you trust, and see cv.cm's article on red flags in a relationship.

sections.h: What is going on when you want them back
body: The first weeks after a breakup are the worst time to make decisions. Missing someone can feel like physical pain, sleep and appetite change, and the mind keeps replaying the relationship. The urge to message is strongest exactly when your judgement is weakest.

Researchers who studied on-again/off-again dating relationships (Dailey and colleagues, 2009) found that partners who had broken up and got back together reported fewer positives, such as love and understanding, and more negatives, such as communication problems and uncertainty, than partners who had never broken up. The more times a couple broke up and renewed, the more negatives they reported. This does not mean a second try always fails. It means a second try only works if something real is different. Getting back together to stop the pain of missing them is not a change.
So the question to ask is not "How do I get them back?" but "What would make a second relationship different from the first, and do they want that too?"

ol: Take space. Stop messaging, calling and liking their posts for a while, usually at least 30 days. This is not a trick to make them miss you. It lets both of you calm down and think. See cv.cm's article on the no contact rule for how to do it.
Understand why it ended. Write down the reasons they gave, in their words. Then write your part and their part separately. If you only have a list of their faults, you are not done yet.

Change what was yours to change. Make it concrete: "I will not go silent for days after a fight", "I will stop drinking on weeknights", "I am seeing a counsellor about my jealousy". Live it for weeks before you mention it. A promise is not a change.
Send one honest message. Short, calm, with no demand and no deadline. Examples are in the next section.
Meet, listen and accept the answer. If they agree to talk, listen more than you speak. Ask what they need. If they say no, thank them and stop.

head: Time after the breakup
Focus
What it looks like
rows: Weeks 1 to 2
Survive and stop contact
Mute and archive the chat, lean on friends, sleep and eat regularly
Weeks 3 to 4
Understand
Write down why it ended; talk it through with a friend or counsellor
Weeks 5 to 8
Change
Work on your part every day; notice if you still want them, or only want the pain to stop
After about 1 to 2 months
Decide
If you still want to try and have something real to offer, send one message; if not, focus on moving on

body: These times are a guide, not a rule. After a long relationship or a marriage you may need longer. If you share a child, a lease or a workplace, keep practical messages short and polite during this time.

sections.h: What to say: one honest message
body: A good message takes responsibility, says what has changed in one sentence, and leaves them free to say no. It does not ask them to reply by a date, and it does not list your pain.

ul: After repeated fights: "Hi. I've been thinking a lot about us. I see now how often I got defensive when you brought things up, and I've been working on that. I would like to talk sometime, if you are open to it. If not, I understand."

After you stopped making an effort: "I know I took you for granted at the end, and I'm sorry. I'm not asking for anything right now. If you would ever like to have a coffee and talk, I would like that."

After you cheated or lied: "I hurt you badly and I'm not going to make excuses. I've started counselling to understand why I did it. If you ever want to talk, I'll listen. If you don't, I will respect that."

head: Message to avoid
Why it backfires
rows: "I can't live without you"
Puts your feelings on them and feels like pressure
"I've changed, I promise" (with nothing specific)
Sounds like every other ex; change shows in actions
"Just give me one more chance"
Asks for a decision before they know anything
Long paragraphs at 2 a.m.
Reads as emotional overflow, not reflection
"Saw you with him. Moved on fast, huh?"
Blame and jealousy end the conversation
"Happy birthday" as a way back in, then silence
Uses a social ritual to test them; they can tell

What it may mean
What to do next

They are open, not committed
Meet in a calm place, listen, do not ask for an answer that day

Maybe later, maybe a soft no

No reply

body: Many "get your ex back" programs teach tactics that are manipulation. They may work for a week. They damage trust, and many are disrespectful or even frightening to the other person.

ul: Do not beg, cry on their doorstep, or send message after message.
Do not try to make them jealous with posts, photos with someone new, or rumors.
Do not show up at their home, work or school uninvited, or wait for them somewhere.
Do not ask their friends or family to pressure them, or pass messages through them.
Do not track their location, check their social media every hour, or make fake accounts to watch them.
Do not flood them with gifts, flowers and big gestures. That is love bombing, not change.
Do not use guilt, threats, or talk of hurting yourself to make them come back.

body.note: If you are having thoughts of hurting yourself after the breakup, please contact a crisis line or emergency services where you live now. This pain is real, and it does get smaller with help and time.

sections.h: How to know when to stop
body: It is time to stop trying and turn toward healing when any of these are true:

ul: They have said no clearly, or asked you not to contact them.
They have blocked you or are in a new relationship.
You sent your one message and a polite follow-up weeks later, with no reply.
You notice you want them back mainly to stop feeling rejected.
The problems that ended it were about safety, respect or control.

body: Stopping is not failing. You did the honest thing, and you can carry what you learned into your next relationship. cv.cm's attachment style test can help you see whether fear of being left, or a habit of pulling away, played a part. When you are ready, see cv.cm's guide on how to get over a breakup.

body.note: If you are in danger, contact local emergency services. For help with an abusive or controlling ex, contact a domestic violence helpline, such as loveisrespect.org or thehotline.org in the US, or a local service where you live.

faq.q: How long should I wait before contacting my ex?
faq.a: There is no magic number, but at least 30 days of no contact is a common starting point, and longer after a long relationship. Wait until you can write a calm message and accept any answer.
Some do, especially when the breakup was about timing or a fixable problem. Many do not. Plan for both outcomes, and do not put your life on hold waiting.

faq.q: Is it a good sign if my ex still texts me?
faq.a: It may mean they miss you, feel lonely, feel guilty, or want to stay friends. Texting alone is not a sign they want the relationship back; ask directly if you need to know.

faq.q: Can I get my ex back if they are with someone new?
faq.a: Trying to break up a new relationship is not respectful and rarely builds anything good. If you want to be honest, you can say once that you would like to talk if they are ever single, then step back.

faq.q: Does the no contact rule make an ex come back?
faq.a: It is not designed to. No contact helps you calm down and think clearly. Some exes do reach out during it, but using silence as a tactic to control their feelings usually shows in later talks.
